newsitem.title: LATVIA: INTERVIEW-DE BROE SAYS MORE TO DO FOR BALTIC BOURSES.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-DE BROE SAYS MORE TO DO FOR BALTIC BOURSES.

text.p: International investment bank Williams De Broe is keen on the Baltic countries' emerging share markets but says they need bigger companies to boost liquidity and attract major foreign players.

"From an international perspective, larger companies and blue chips are needed on the Baltic bourses," Petri Karjalainen, the managing director of Wiliams De Broe's Baltic markets unit, told Reuters at a Baltic investment conference on Wednesday.
All three Baltic markets have experienced volatility this year and have different levels of liquidity.
"There was a liquidity-driven push in Estonia earlier this year...a lot of local investors made a profit which they subsequently recycled into the market," he said.
Liquidity was still lacking in Latvia and Lithuania, he said.
"Latvia's market is still peanuts...it needs to have at least 10 new big companies before it will take off," he said.
He added that while Lithuania's market was still relatively illiquid it offered investors a broader range of opportunities and had lots of potential for growth.
"Lithuania has the scope...it has a good variety of companies and there is a lot of value there," he said.
"It just takes a lot of work to examine them and make the right decisions," he said.
He added that shares in Lithuania's banking sector, which seems to have recovered from a serious crisis, looked very interesting and seemed set to rise.
A strong manufacturing base also bodes well for Lithuania's market though he said that a strong dollar was presently pinching exports. The litas is pegged to the dollar.
"One of the keys in all three countries is that they must be clear about what they intend do with their currency pegs," he said.
